destinations: Agent destination — per-agent routing entry and ACL. Each row authorizes an agent to send messages to a target (channel or another agent) and assigns a local name the agent uses to address it. Names are scoped to the source agent — two agents can have different local names for the same target. Created automatically when wiring channels or when agents create child agents.

Verbs:
  list — List destinations with resolved channel/title labels.
  add [approval] — Add a destination for an agent. Use --agent-group-id, --local-name, --target-type, --target-id.
  remove [approval] — Remove a destination from an agent. Use --agent-group-id and --local-name.

Run `ncl destinations help <verb>` (or add --help to any command) for flags and examples.

Fields:
  --agent-group-id             The agent that owns this destination. References agent_groups.id.
  --local-name                 Name the agent uses to address this target (e.g. send_message({ to: "local_name", ... })). Unique per agent. Lowercase, dash-separated.
  --target-type                "channel" for messaging group targets, "agent" for agent-to-agent targets. (values: channel | agent)
  --target-id                  The target's ID — messaging_groups.id for channels, agent_groups.id for agents.
  --channel-type               Resolved channel type for channel destinations.
  --display-name               Resolved chat title or agent name.
  --created-at                 Auto-set.
